title: Snow and gales cancel Jeju flights and ferries
detail: Heavy snow and wind advisories led to 17 flight cancellations and 29 delays at Jeju airport by 13:00, and six ferry services including Jeju–Wando and Jeju–Chuja were cancelled, per Korea Airports Corporation and KMA figures.
agency: Korea Airports Corporation; Korea Meteorological Administration
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Airports Corporation and KMA

title: North Korea fires first ballistic missiles of 2026 from Pyongyang
detail: JCS detected multiple projectiles launched from Pyongyang's Ryokpho district flying about 900-950 km into the East Sea; North Korea claimed hypersonic missiles overseen by Kim Jong Un, per USNI News.
attribution: USNI News citing ROK JCS, KCNA and Japan MOD

title: North Korea says drone from Ganghwa crashed near Kaesong
detail: Pyongyang said a South Korean drone flew into its airspace on Jan 4, launched from Songhae township on Ganghwa Island and crashing in Kaepung District near Kaesong; Seoul denied military involvement and opened a joint military-police probe, per Korea Times.
attribution: Korea Times citing DPRK claims and ROK Ministry of National Defense

title: Black-ice crashes kill five on Seosan–Yeongdeok Expressway
detail: A series of black-ice crashes on the Sangju section before dawn killed five people, including four occupants of one sedan; police estimated more than 20 vehicles were involved and traffic was temporarily restricted.
attribution: The Korea Herald citing police

title: Uiseong wildfire main blaze put out within three hours
detail: A wildfire broke out around 15:15 in Uiseong County; a Level 2 response was issued, residents were told to move to village halls, and 10 helicopters and 315 personnel contained it by about 18:00, per Korea Herald.
attribution: Korea Herald citing Gyeongbuk Fire Service Headquarters

title: Seoul city bus strike halts most of the fleet for two days
detail: The Seoul city bus union struck from 04:00 on Jan. 13, idling about 93% of the fleet (around 6,540 buses), until a deal late on Jan. 15 gave a 2.9% raise; service resumed the next morning. The city said emergency subway and shuttle measures cost about 10 billion won a day.
attribution: The Korea Herald; cost figure per Seoul city officials

title: Customs busts Chinese-run ring laundering 148.9 billion won via crypto
detail: Korea Customs Service said three Chinese nationals laundered about 148.9 billion won (~US$101.7 million) from 2021 to mid-2025 by buying crypto abroad, moving it through Korean wallets and cashing out via Korean bank accounts disguised as medical or tuition payments.
attribution: Korea Times citing Korea Customs Service

title: 73 Korean scam suspects repatriated from Cambodia
detail: 73 South Koreans were flown from Phnom Penh to Incheon on a Korean Air charter to face probes; police allege about 48.6 billion won (~US$33.6 million) was taken from about 869 victims via romance and investment scams run from seven identified compounds, per UPI.
attribution: UPI citing Korean National Police Agency

title: Probe raids NIS and Army Intelligence Command over drone flights into North
detail: A military-police joint task force searched 18 locations including the NIS and Army Intelligence Command; three active-duty officers were booked and three civilians charged over drones allegedly flown into North Korea, per UPI.
attribution: UPI

title: Hamyang wildfire burns 234 ha in 44 hours
detail: A wildfire that started around 21:00 burned 234 hectares in Hamyang County before being contained after about 44 hours; 164 residents evacuated. The Korea Forest Service raised a Level 2 response and 115 helicopters were mobilised.
agency: Korea Forest Service; National Fire Agency
attribution: The Korea Times citing the Korea Forest Service

title: Miryang wildfire burns 124 ha; 184 evacuated
detail: A wildfire that began about 16:00 in Miryang damaged at least 124 hectares and was 51% contained by the next morning; 184 people including care-hospital patients were evacuated and the National Fire Agency issued a national mobilization order.
agency: National Fire Agency / Korea Forest Service
attribution: Korea Herald citing National Fire Agency and Korea Forest Service

title: Ring smuggled 900,000 cigarette packs to Australia, NZ and UK
detail: Incheon customs referred 11 suspects over about 70 shipments of 900,000 packs (570,000 counterfeit) mislabelled as goods such as rubber mats, earning about 10 billion won (~US$6.78 million), per Korea Herald.
agency: Incheon Main Customs, Korea Customs Service
attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Customs Service

title: Ultrafine dust alert as Chinese wildfire smoke reaches Seoul area
detail: A 'concern' level ultrafine dust disaster alert was issued at 17:00. Sunday with emergency reduction measures on Monday for the Seoul area and South Chungcheong as smoke from wildfires in northeast China drifted in, per Seoul Economic Daily citing NIER.
agency: Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment / NIER
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing National Institute of Environmental Research

title: FIU fines Bithumb 36.8 billion won over AML breaches
detail: The Financial Intelligence Unit fined crypto exchange Bithumb 36.8 billion won (~US$24.6 million) for about 6.65 million AML violations including KYC failures, and ordered a six-month partial suspension for new users; a court later lifted the suspension.
attribution: CoinDesk citing Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

title: Signal failure halts Line 9 express trains
detail: A signal failure detected at 10:22 forced all Seoul Subway Line 9 express trains to run as local services for about two hours until 12:17; the cause was under investigation.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the operator

title: Daejeon auto parts factory fire kills 14, injures 60
detail: Fire broke out around 13:17 at an auto parts plant in Daedeok District, killing 14 and injuring 60; nine victims were found in an illegally built rest area and police, NFS and the labor ministry are investigating the cause.
agency: Daejeon Metropolitan Police Agency / National Fire Agency
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing fire and police authorities

title: Three civilians indicted over drone incursion into North Korea
detail: Seoul Central District Prosecutors' Office indicted three civilians linked to a drone company for 'general benefiting of the enemy' and Aviation Safety Act violations over drone flights into the North, per NK News.
attribution: NK News citing prosecutors

title: President Lee expresses regret to North over January drone incursion
detail: President Lee Jae Myung expressed regret to North Korea for tensions caused by the January drone flight after Seoul's probe found NIS officials and an active-duty officer were involved, per Malay Mail.
attribution: Malay Mail

title: Gale-force winds batter Jeju; KMA records 28.9 m/s on Udo
detail: KMA recorded winds of 28.9 m/s on Udo and 27.2 m/s at Jeju airport; high-wave warnings halted island ferries and 20-30 mm/h rain was forecast into the next morning, per The Star.
attribution: The Star citing KMA

title: 246 flights cancelled at Jeju airport, 3,000+ stranded
detail: By 19:00 246 flights (12 international) were cancelled and 83 delayed at Jeju International Airport due to strong winds, stranding over 3,000 passengers; island ferries were also suspended.
attribution: The Star

title: FIU fines Coinone 5.2 billion won, partial suspension
detail: The FIU fined exchange Coinone 5.2 billion won (~US$3.49 million) for failing to verify about 70,000 users and facilitating around 10,000 transactions with 16 unregistered overseas exchanges, plus a three-month partial suspension.
attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Financial Intelligence Unit

title: Laotian worker arrested over 5 kg meth shipped from Thailand
detail: Customs' Gwangju office arrested a Lao national who received 5 kg of methamphetamine hidden in snack and coffee bags shipped from Thailand to Yongin in February; the alleged ringleader remains at large.
attribution: Korea Herald citing Korea Customs Service

title: FX task force uncovers 600 billion won in illegal transactions incl. hwanchigi
detail: A government-wide illegal FX response team (NIS, NTS, BOK, FSS) uncovered over 600 billion won in four months, including a remittance firm using 25,000 virtual accounts to launder gambling proceeds (400 billion won) and a used-car exporter paid in crypto cashed out via hwanchigi brokers (200 billion won).
attribution: Kyunghyang Shinmun citing government FX response team

title: Korean man with disability freed from Sihanoukville captivity
detail: A Korean man in his 30s with a disability, lured by a social-media job post, was held in a Sihanoukville hotel, abused and threatened with a US$20,000 ransom; he was freed on May 7, per Korean National Police Agency.
agency: Korean National Police Agency / Korea-Cambodia Korean Desk
attribution: Korea Times citing Korean National Police Agency

title: Korean Desk rescues woman held for ransom in Phnom Penh
detail: The Korea-Cambodia joint police task force (Korean Desk) rescued a Korean woman in her 20s held captive after travelling to meet an online contact, and arrested a Chinese suspect, per KNPA.
agency: Korean National Police Agency / Korea-Cambodia Korean Desk
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korean National Police Agency

title: Earliest-ever heat-related death recorded in Seoul
detail: KDCA reported a man in Seoul died of heat-related illness on May 16, the earliest such case on record, a day after it began surveillance at 516 emergency rooms; seven heat patients were treated the previous day.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KDCA

title: 24 African swine fever farm cases confirmed in seven provinces
detail: The agriculture ministry confirmed 24 ASF cases between Jan 16 and Mar 16 across seven provinces including Gyeonggi (Pocheon, Yeoncheon) and Gangwon; standstill orders were lifted Apr 22 but alerts remain for 32 cities and counties.
agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs
attribution: Korea Times citing Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

title: Overpass under demolition collapses in Seodaemun, 3 dead
detail: A section of a 1966-built overpass being demolished in Seoul's Seodaemun District gave way, killing three workers and injuring three; debris fell on nearby tracks, per AP via ABC News.
attribution: AP citing fire and police officials

title: Korail suspends some Seoul Station services after overpass collapse
detail: Korea Railroad Corp. suspended some operations into Seoul Station after debris from a collapsed overpass fell onto tracks in Seodaemun District; local roads were sealed off.
attribution: AP

title: Soil collapse kills worker at Gangnam sewer site
detail: A 3.5-metre pile of soil collapsed at a sewer maintenance site near Suseo Station, killing a worker in his 60s; a labour office official said no retaining wall had been installed.
attribution: The Korea Herald citing a labour office official

title: Cambodian court jails six Chinese for life over scam-linked killing of Korean student
detail: Kampot Provincial Court sentenced six Chinese nationals to life for murder, unlawful detention, torture and organised fraud over the 2025 death of a Korean university student lured to Cambodia by a scam ring, per Korea Times.
attribution: Korea Times

title: Explosion at Hanwha Aerospace Daejeon plant kills five
detail: An explosion at 10:59 while workers cleaned explosive residue from rocket-propellant tooling killed five and injured two; the cause was under investigation and executives could face probes under the Serious Accidents Punishment Act.
agency: National Fire Agency; Ministry of Employment and Labor
attribution: The Korea Times citing police, fire authorities and the company

title: Tropical Storm Jangmi disrupts Incheon and Gimpo flights
detail: AirHelp flight data showed 20 cancellations and 120 delays at Incheon and 12 cancellations and 48 delays at Gimpo on June 3 as Tropical Storm Jangmi affected the region.
attribution: AirHelp flight-disruption data (aggregator)

title: 23 charged for laundering Cambodia phishing proceeds via USDT
detail: Seoul police referred 23 suspects (two detained) for laundering about 16.8 billion won (~US$11.1 million) for a Cambodia-based phishing group by cycling USDT through domestic and overseas exchanges; the alleged ringleader is under an Interpol Red Notice, per Decrypt.
attribution: Decrypt citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

title: Nationwide Japanese encephalitis alert after virus found in Daegu mosquito
detail: KDCA issued a nationwide Japanese encephalitis alert after detecting the virus in a Culex mosquito in Daegu, earlier than last year's Aug 1 alert, and urged local larval control.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KDCA

title: Car mounts Busan sidewalk, killing two pedestrians
detail: A car driven by a man in his 70s struck four pedestrians on a sidewalk in Nam District, killing two women and injuring two; police said the driver claimed sudden unintended acceleration and the cause was under investigation.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing police

title: Trawler Dong-a No. 3 collides with gas carrier off Busan
detail: The 79-ton trawler collided with a gas carrier about 24 nautical miles southeast of Daebyeon Port, Gijang; five of eight crew were rescued, one died and two were missing. Oceans Minister Hwang Jong-woo ordered an all-out search.
agency: Ulsan Coast Guard; Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries
attribution: The Herald Business citing the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries

title: Over 10 Chinese and Russian military aircraft enter KADIZ
detail: JCS said more than 10 Chinese and Russian military aircraft entered and left the KADIZ over the East Sea and off the south coast during an apparent joint drill without violating territorial airspace; ROK fighters were scrambled.
attribution: Korea Herald citing ROK JCS

title: WeTax and Gov24 local tax services down for 12 hours
detail: The Interior Ministry said a surge in data traffic during a system update knocked out WeTax, Gov24, civil-service kiosks and the local tax network for about 12 hours; services were restored by 20:50 and tax deadlines were extended.
agency: Ministry of the Interior and Safety
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the Ministry of the Interior and Safety

title: M2.1 quake near Gimcheon felt in two provinces
detail: KMA reported a magnitude 2.1 earthquake 13 km northeast of Gimcheon at 9 km depth, with max intensity III in North Gyeongsang; no significant damage reported.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing KMA

title: First repatriation of Korean scam members from Malaysia
detail: Two Korean members of a Malaysia-based 'no-show' fraud ring were arrested at Kuala Lumpur International Airport on July 7 and repatriated, the first such case from Malaysia, per Seoul Economic Daily.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing police

title: Power failure paralyses Seoul Subway Line 1 at rush hour
detail: A power outage at 07:29 halted southbound Line 1 trains between Changdong and Sinimun; power returned at 09:48 and service at 09:57, causing heavy congestion along the line. Korail said the cause was under investigation.
attribution: The Korea Times citing Korail

title: Monsoon downpours hit Chungcheong; one missing, 758 evacuated
detail: Heavy rain on July 9-10 dropped 267.1 mm on Cheonan and 259 mm on Gyeryong; a man in his 70s was swept away in Yeongju, 758 people were evacuated nationwide and over 450 facilities damaged, per the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters.
agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

title: Five landslides in North Chungcheong and Gangwon during monsoon rain
detail: Five landslides were reported in North Chungcheong and eastern Gangwon during July 9-10 rain, with no casualties, per the disaster headquarters.
agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

title: Man in his 70s swept away by rapid current in Yeongju
detail: A man in his 70s went missing after being swept away by a fast-flowing stream in Yeongju during heavy rain, per disaster authorities.
agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

title: Heavy rain blocks Dongbu Expressway entrance in Seoul
detail: Overnight rain of 117.9 mm in Seoul and over 150 mm in northern Gyeonggi blocked the entrance to the Dongbu Expressway; the Korea Forest Service issued landslide warnings for the whole Greater Seoul area at 06:00.
agency: Korea Meteorological Administration; Korea Forest Service
attribution: The Korea Herald citing KMA and the Korea Forest Service

title: Torrential rain floods Seoul, Gyeonggi and Daegu
detail: Overnight rain reached 166 mm in Eunpyeong (64.5 mm/h in Seodaemun) and 183.5 mm in Daegu's Jisan-dong; Seoul issued flood warnings for Gangseo, Eunpyeong and Mapo, and people were rescued from flooded homes in Paju and Gumi and stranded vehicles in Daegu.
agency: Seoul Metropolitan Government; Korea Meteorological Administration; Korea Forest Service
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KMA, Seoul city and the Korea Forest Service

title: Rain triggers 540 landslides and rockfalls; one missing in Yeongwol
detail: Up to 197.5 mm in Paju and 171.1 mm in Cheorwon caused 793 facility damage cases including 540 landslides and rockfalls; 294 people were in shelters and a fisher went missing in the Jucheon River in Yeongwol, per the disaster headquarters.
agency: Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasures Headquarters

title: Customs seizes record 1,007 kg of drugs in first half
detail: Korea Customs Service caught 767 smuggling cases totaling 1,007 kg in H1 2026 (654 kg cannabis, 230 kg meth, 58 kg ketamine), with Thailand the top origin; 717 offenders were caught including 14 teenagers.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Customs Service

title: Customs uncovers 7.2 trillion won in illegal FX dealings in H1
detail: Korea Customs Service said it uncovered 792 illegal foreign-exchange cases worth 7.2 trillion won (~US$4.9 billion) in H1 2026, including unauthorised transfers, hidden overseas assets and export proceeds received in crypto.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Customs Service

title: Miryang restricts supply at 39 of 40 farm reservoirs
detail: Miryang moved 39 of its 40 agricultural reservoirs to every-other-day supply; Maheul and Baegan reservoirs were near empty and Miryang Dam was at 34.6%, per Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Rural Community Corporation.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Rural Community Corporation

title: 50-metre section of Pohang sea bridge collapses
detail: About 50 metres of the 225-metre Boritdol pedestrian sea bridge in Guryongpo-eup fell into the sea; all 17 anglers on it were rescued within 12 minutes. The bridge had been repaired in 2025–26 but was not subject to mandatory safety inspections.
attribution: SBS News

title: Unmun Dam at 27.3% as drought exposes submerged village
detail: Unmun Dam storage stood at 27.3%, exposing a village submerged for 41 years; North Gyeongsang reservoirs averaged 58.2% against a normal 71.6%, and Miryang's Baekan Reservoir held about 1.2%.
attribution: The Kyunghyang Shinmun

title: Bohyeonsan Dam storage falls to 16.4% as southern drought worsens
detail: The National Drought Information Portal put Bohyeonsan Dam storage at 16.4% amid prolonged heat and below-average rain across southern regions, per Korea Herald.
attribution: Korea Herald citing National Drought Information Portal

title: Ulsan's Daegok Dam falls to 8.1%; river water piped in
detail: Daegok Dam fell to 8.1% of capacity and Ulsan began drawing water from the Nakdong River 40 km away; Miryang and Changnyeong began supply restrictions and Cheongdo stockpiled bottled water.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily

title: National record 42.5C set in Yangsan
detail: KMA confirmed 42.5C in Yangsan at 13:26, the highest temperature on record in Korea; Yangsan exceeded 40C five days running and more than 20 localities were under the new emergency heat alert, per ABC News.
attribution: ABC News citing KMA

title: Record 186 heat-illness cases in a day; two suspected deaths in Wanju
detail: KDCA logged 186 heat-related illness cases on Aug 3, the year's daily high, bringing the total to 2,221 with 19 suspected deaths; two elderly people with underlying conditions died in Wanju, per Korea Herald.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Korea Herald citing KDCA and KMA

title: Heat-driven apartment blackouts hit Incheon, Goyang, Seoul
detail: Overloaded transformers and wiring amid the heat wave cut power to 374 households in Gyeyang, Incheon for over four hours and 460 in Deogyang, Goyang for two hours, with outages also in Gangseo, Seoul and Suwon, per JoongAng Daily.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing local authorities

title: First SFTS death of 2026 reported on Jeju
detail: Korea reported its first severe fever with thrombocytopenia syndrome (tick-borne) death of 2026 on Jeju on Aug 5; Seoul expanded tick surveillance and found no SFTS virus in about 480 ticks, per Korea Times.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Korea Times citing Seoul Research Institute of Public Health and Environment

title: North Korea fires SRBM from Wonsan toward East Sea
detail: JCS said it detected a short-range ballistic missile launched from the Wonsan area around 17:00; it was the first known SRBM test in about five months, per NK News.
attribution: NK News citing ROK JCS

title: 81 mm/h downpour floods Gangneung roads
detail: A cloudburst of 81.4 mm/h in Gangneung's Yonggang-dong briefly submerged roads; seven vacationers were rescued near Baekdamsa in Inje and a multi-vehicle crash near Daegwallyeong Tunnel injured three. Gangneung raised its disaster headquarters to Level 2.
attribution: The Kyunghyang Shinmun citing KMA and Gangneung City

title: Crow contact causes back-to-back outages in Busan's Buk District
detail: About 986 households in Hwamyeong- and Geumgok-dong lost power on Aug 8 and 981 in Gupo-dong on Aug 9 for about an hour each; Busan city blamed a crow touching equipment, per JoongAng Daily.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Busan city and KEPCO

title: Three rescued after motorboat capsizes off Ongjin
detail: Incheon Coast Guard rescued three men clinging to a capsized 0.28-ton motorboat near Choji Island about 11 hours after they lost contact on a fishing trip; all were stable.
attribution: Korea Herald citing Incheon Coast Guard

title: Okcheon Reservoir surface shrinks 89% in drought
detail: Satellite imagery showed Okcheon Reservoir in Changnyeong down 88.8% in surface area from a year earlier; agricultural reservoirs averaged 53.2% nationwide and 39.6% in South Gyeongsang as of Aug. 3, and water trucks were supplying farms.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily; satellite figures from analyst TelePIX
value_unit: % avg agricultural reservoir storage, South Gyeongsang

title: Typhoon Chan-hom to bring east-coast rain but no direct hit
detail: KMA said Typhoon Chan-hom (No. 15), near Tokyo, would not directly affect Korea but easterly flow could bring 20-60 mm to the east coast and 10-40 mm to South Gyeongsang on Aug 12-13, likely insufficient to ease the southern drought.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KMA

title: Philippines-based ring used porn sites to drive 4.7 trillion won in illegal bets
detail: Seoul police detained two men accused of running a Pasay City-based network whose own illegal pornography sites funnelled users to 18 gambling sites, with 4.7 trillion won wagered and 47.6 billion won (~US$34 million) in profits since 2019.
attribution: Korea Herald citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

title: Miryang, Geoje and Haman hit 'severe' drought stage
detail: Seoul Economic Daily reported Miryang, Geoje and Haman reached the severe drought stage, with agricultural drought alerts in 17 of 18 South Gyeongsang municipalities, reservoirs at 33.3% (normal 71.3%) and about 2,121 ha of crops affected; water was rationed in 26 villages.
agency: National Fire Agency / South Gyeongsang Province
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily

title: Bangkok-based sextortion phishing ring busted
detail: Seoul police with Thai police apprehended 11 members of a Bangkok call centre that impersonated officials and extorted 68 Koreans with nude photos, taking 6.7 billion won (~US$4.73 million); nine Korean members remain at large in Thailand.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

title: 159 fire tankers mobilized to supply water to drought-hit South Gyeongsang
detail: Fire authorities extended a national mobilization order, sending 159 water tankers (100 from other provinces) that delivered 12,445 tons in two days; provincial reservoir storage averaged 32.2% versus a 70.6% norm, per Korea Times.
agency: National Fire Agency / Ministry of the Interior and Safety
attribution: Korea Times citing fire authorities and interior ministry

title: Scaffolding contact cuts power to 251 Mapo households
detail: A power line contacted by construction scaffolding cut electricity to 251 households in Seogyo-dong at 18:52 during the heat wave; KEPCO partly restored supply by 19:41.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing KEPCO

title: Record deluge in Geoje and Tongyeong triggers floods and landslides
detail: Three-day rain from Aug 16 reached 851.1 mm in Geoje (124.5 mm in one hour) and 704.8 mm in Tongyeong; one person died, four were injured, about 160 evacuated and 136 rescued by firefighters, per Korea Herald. A landslide engulfed the first floor of an apartment building in Okpo-dong, Geoje.
attribution: Korea Herald citing KMA and fire authorities

title: Warning shots after North Korean soldiers cross MDL on eastern front
detail: The South Korean military fired warning shots after multiple North Korean soldiers crossed the Military Demarcation Line on the eastern front the previous week; they returned north. It was the first such warning fire of 2026, per Korea Herald.
attribution: Korea Herald citing military/government sources

title: Landslide hits apartment building in Okpo-dong, Geoje
detail: During the southeastern deluge a landslide engulfed the first floor of an apartment building in Okpo-dong around 04:32; multiple other landslides blocked roads, per Korea Herald.
attribution: Korea Herald

title: Coast guard: 31 Chinese caught entering illegally via Taean coast since 2019
detail: The Coast Guard said 31 Chinese nationals were caught entering by small or rubber boats at Taean between Sept 2019 and May 2026, 25 of them previously deported workers; attempts peak in calm seas in spring and autumn.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Korea Coast Guard

title: Police and China bust China-based voice phishing ring
detail: Gangwon police with Jilin public security arrested 10 (6 Korean, 4 Chinese) accused of taking about 10 billion won (~US$7.23 million) from 118 mostly elderly Koreans in 2025-26 by impersonating officials and planting malicious apps; proceeds were split in crypto.
attribution: Korea Times citing Gangwon Provincial Police Agency

title: Chungbuk police bust Vietnam-based gambling site with 63 billion won in bets
detail: Chungbuk police referred 13 operators and 105 users of a Vietnam-run baccarat, slots and sports-betting site that took 63 billion won (~US$46 million) in bets from 3,553 users; 186.35 million won was frozen and a ringleader is at large.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Chungbuk Provincial Police Agency

title: Heat-related illnesses near 3,800 with 34 deaths
detail: KDCA surveillance counted nearly 3,800 heat-related illness cases and 34 deaths this summer as of Aug 27, led by Gyeonggi (925), Seoul (457) and South Gyeongsang (322); level-4 heat risk alert remained in effect.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KDCA

title: KMA: Krovanh expected to stall near Okinawa; fall typhoon risk rising
detail: KMA said Typhoon Krovanh (No. 24) should be pushed back by high pressure north of Korea; no typhoon hit Korea in summer 2026 despite 17 forming nearby, and experts warned fall paths toward Korea could open, per JoongAng Daily.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing KMA

title: Tugboat capsizes off Busan; one dead, six missing
detail: The 286-ton tugboat TNS Catcher capsized about 9 km southeast of Oryukdo with eight crew; one Indonesian crew member was rescued, one Korean crew member was found dead and six were missing. The Busan Coast Guard deployed 13 vessels and President Lee Jae Myung ordered all resources mobilised.
attribution: The Korea Herald citing the Busan Coast Guard

title: Typhoon Krovanh winds delay 84 Jeju flights, halt ferries
detail: Wind shear and high-wind advisories linked to Typhoon Krovanh delayed 84 of 505 scheduled flights at Jeju airport; ferries to Jindo and Samcheonpo and all services to Gapado and Marado were suspended, per the Jeju weather office and Korea Airports Corporation.
agency: Korea Airports Corporation; Jeju Regional Office of Meteorology
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Korea Airports Corporation and the Jeju weather office

title: Typhoon Krovanh gales kill one at Jeju Port
detail: Gales from Typhoon Krovanh reached 26.9 m/s at Saebyeol Oreum; a man in his 50s died when a crane collapsed at Jeju Port and others were hurt, 184 flights were delayed and island ferries suspended, per Herald Business.
attribution: Herald Business citing KMA, coast guard and fire authorities

title: North Korean troops crossed MDL more than 20 times in a month
detail: JCS said North Korean troops crossed the MDL over 20 times in the past month, mostly on one eastern-front section during DMZ construction work, exceeding 17 in all of 2025; the military fired warning shots and asked the UN Command to investigate.
agency: ROK Joint Chiefs of Staff / UN Command
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing JCS and UNC

title: First human Japanese encephalitis case of 2026 confirmed
detail: KDCA confirmed the year's first Japanese encephalitis case in an unvaccinated woman in her 60s who fell ill around Aug 15, warning September-October is peak season, per Seoul Economic Daily.
agency: Korea Disease Control and Prevention Agency
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing KDCA

title: North Korea fires several ballistic missiles from Wonsan
detail: JCS detected several ballistic missiles launched from the Wonsan area around 05:20 that flew about 250 km, a day after US-ROK-Japan maritime drills ended, per Al Jazeera.
attribution: Al Jazeera citing ROK JCS

title: Gyeonggi police bust shell-company laundering ring for fraud gangs
detail: Gyeonggi Nambu police arrested seven, including the ringleader, accused of laundering 93.4 billion won (~US$67 million) in fraud proceeds from mid-2024 to Feb 2026 through fake gift-certificate distributors in Seoul and Gyeonggi.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Gyeonggi Nambu Provincial Police Agency

title: 15 ground-subsidence cases on Seoul roads so far in 2026
detail: MOLIT's underground safety information system logged 15 sinkhole cases in Seoul through Sept. 15, after 42 in 2025; about 40% of 2021–2025 cases were linked to sewer damage. Recent holes opened near Suyu and Gongdeok stations and in Jegi-dong without injuries.
agency: Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing MOLIT data

title: Ministry tightens winter controls on bird flu, FMD and ASF
detail: MAFRA said 21 of 2026's 24 ASF cases were linked to contaminated plasma-protein feed, overseas wild-bird flu cases doubled to 2,957, and a new SAT1 FMD strain is in China and Mongolia; 280 control zones will run Oct-Feb.
agency: Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs

title: 462 Koreans arrested in six Southeast Asian countries in H1; rings shift to Malaysia
detail: Foreign ministry data showed 462 Koreans arrested for transnational crimes in six Southeast Asian countries in H1 2026, 4.6 times the prior year; rings have moved to Malaysia, Thailand, Vietnam and Kazakhstan, incl. a Bac Ninh ring that took about 24.3 billion won from 630+ small-business owners.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Ministry of Foreign Affairs

title: 30 arrested in ring hiding meth in sunflower-seed packets
detail: Seoul police arrested 30 (17 detained) over drugs worth about 6 billion won (~US$4.3 million), including 1.25 kg meth and 500 g ketamine smuggled from Cambodia, the Philippines and Thailand via Incheon airport; three overseas leaders are on Interpol red notices.
attribution: Seoul Economic Daily citing Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency

title: Contaminated tank cuts water to ~5,000 Suwon apartments
detail: Tap water smelling of paint thinner cut supply to about 5,000 households in a Jangan-gu apartment complex for over 12 hours; management blamed epoxy waterproofing work on the tank and the city sent water tankers.
attribution: SBS News citing apartment management and district officials

title: North Korea fires two projectiles from Wonsan within three hours
detail: JCS detected an SRBM (possibly Hwasong-11 type) from the Wonsan area around 15:00 that flew about 450 km, and a second projectile around 18:00; it followed a Sept 12 launch, per JoongAng Daily.
attribution: Korea JoongAng Daily citing ROK JCS

title: Workers at three Korail subsidiaries begin three-day strike
detail: About 1,300 workers at Korail Networks, Korail Tourism Development and the railway customer centre struck against a plan to merge five subsidiaries into three, according to the union (police estimated 800 at the rally). No major train cancellations were reported in the article.
attribution: SBS News; turnout per union, rally figure per police estimate

title: Apartment fire in Gangnam's Suseo-dong forces 60 to evacuate
detail: A fire at an apartment building in Suseo-dong around 12:10 forced 60 residents to evacuate and one was treated for smoke inhalation; about 200 firefighters put it out in 1 hour 20 minutes, per SBS.
attribution: SBS citing fire authorities

title: Chuseok traffic: Seoul–Busan trip over 7 hours
detail: Korea Expressway Corp. estimated 6.84 million vehicles on the roads on Chuseok day; at 14:00. Busan to Seoul took 8 hours 10 minutes and Seoul to Busan 7 hours 20 minutes. Tolls were waived Sept. 24–27.
attribution: The Korea Times citing Korea Expressway Corp.

title: Bird contact cuts power to 578 Yangju households
detail: A bird touching high-voltage equipment caused an outage in Samsung-dong and Mansong-dong around 11:00; KEPCO restored power in about an hour.
attribution: SBS News citing KEPCO
